newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks fall 2.61 pct on baht worries.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks fall 2.61 pct on baht worries.

text.p: Thai stocks declined 2.61 percent at 0835 GMT on Monday as investors unloaded large capitalised stocks on worries about the weakness of Thai baht, brokers said.
The composite SET index fell 2.61 percent or 16.39 points to 612.16 by 0835 GMT.
The market recouped slightly to 613.52 in thin dealings by 0845 GMT.

"Investors are selling some bank, finance, communication and energy issues on worries about the sliding baht and an intervention by the central bank to defend the currency," said Witawus Charuchandr of Ekachart Finance and Securities.
Bank of Thailand Governor Rerngchai Marakanond confirmed market talk and said that his bank had intervened by selling dollars to help stem the baht's fall against the dollar.
